title: Comic Market: Ticketpay Service Restricts Access for International Users
content:
The staff for the Comic Market ( Comiket ) dōjinshi event in Japan reported on Wednesday that the Japanese ticketing service Ticketpay is banning access from users outside of Japan "for the forseeable future to guard against cyberattacks." This restriction would block international users from entering the lottery to purchase tickets for Comiket 109 next month, as well as other future events that use the ticketing service.

The event staff noted that they are currently investigating alternative methods for people outside of Japan to purchase tickets, but added that given the short timeframe between the announcement and the event's opening on December 29, finding a solution will be difficult.

Comiket 109 will take place at Tokyo Big Sight from December 29 to 31.

Comiket 108 ran on August 15 to 16 earlier this year, and drew 260,000 attendees.

The first Comiket drew an estimated 700 attendees for 32 exhibiting circles in December 1975. Tokyo's Harumi area, Chiba's Makuhari Messe venue, and other places hosted the event before it moved to its current Tokyo Big Sight location for Comiket 50 in 1996.

The event has historically been free for general attendees, but began charging a fee in August 2019 due to a temporary venue change caused by preparations for the Summer Olympics in Tokyo. It then began selling tickets to limit attendance in the first in-person event during the COVID-19 pandemic in December 2021. It stopped limiting its attendance in August 2023, but continuing charging for tickets to general attendees.

title: Yuri Is My Job! Manga Gets Short Drama Adaptation Next Spring
content:
Donuts announced on Friday that its vertical content streaming app Tatedora is producing a live-action short adaptation of Miman 's Yuri Is My Job! ( Watashi no Yuri wa Oshigoto Desu! ) manga that will debut on the service in spring 2027. Daiki Nakayama is directing the project, with scripts by Nishioka To Neil.

Kodansha USA Publishing is releasing the manga in English, and it describes the story:

Hime is a picture-perfect high school princess—she's admired by all and never trips up! So when she accidentally injures a café manager named Mai, she's willing to cover some shifts to keep her facade intact. To Hime's surprise, the café is themed after a private school where the all-female staff always puts on their best act for their loyal customers. However, under the guidance of the most graceful girl there, Hime can't help but blush and blunder! Beneath all the frills and laughter, Hime feels tension brewing as she finds out more about her new job and her budding feelings 

Miman launched the manga in Ichijinsha 's Comic Yuri Hime magazine in November 2016, and Ichijinsha published the 13th volume in Japan in January 2024. The 14th and 15th volume will release simultaneously on November 18. Kodansha USA Publishing released the 13th volume in English in January 2025.

The manga inspired a television anime that premiered in April 2023. Crunchyroll streamed the anime as it aired in Japan.

title: Jujutsu Kaisen Needs Another Sequel to Fix Its Biggest Mistakes That Can Save the Series
content:
The Jujutsu Kaisen manga reached its controversial ending in September 2024, leaving behind several unanswered questions. The final battle went on for over a year, but the ending didn’t resolve several plot points . Only a year after the confusing finale, Gege Akutami returned with a sequel manga that completely turned the world of Jujutsu Kaisen upside down. While Akutami served as the series’ writer, Yuji Iwasaki provided the gorgeous illustrations that fans can’t stop praising. The story takes place 68 years after the Culling Game, following new characters, including the grandchildren of Yuta Okkotsu, who were introduced in the epilogue. The world is far from peaceful since the threat of the cursed spirits never ceased to exist.

However, the most shocking part of the sequel is how it explores sci-fi themes with aliens, also known as Simurians, who came to Japan as refugees. As the story continued, it focused primarily on the struggles between the sorcerers and the Simurians as their differences made it all the more impossible for them to co-exist. However, the sci-fi twist was more crucial than fans initially realized since it solved the biggest problem in the world of curses.

Jujutsu Kaisen Modulo’ s Ending Changed the World Forever

There’s no denying that the world of curses only caused suffering to everyone living in it, regardless of whether they were sorcerers or ordinary citizens. Sorcerers were only a few in number, while the curses were unbelievably powerful, and they continued to manifest due to negative emotions. By the time the story reached its finale, Maru, a Simurian, joined hands with Yuji to rid the world of curses .

This is something that the original story teased but couldn’t delve deep into since the sorcerers already had their hands full fighting the villains. However, the fight between Yuka and Dabura could only end with the girl surviving if Maru performed the Harmony Ritual. This never would’ve been possible if not for his powers as well as Yuji’s help. The ending not only created a much safer and more stable world, but also confirmed that aliens have been accepted into society. Despite everything that happened, the challenges that come with reshaping the world of curses are far more severe. However, since Yuji has a long life ahead of him since he has become something like a half-curse and half-human, he will continue his journey to permanently eradicate cursed spirits and the root cause of cursed energy.

Jujutsu Kaisen Still Has Several Unanswered Questions That Might Never Be Resolved

Only a year after the manga finale, Akutami returned with a sequel story, Jujutsu Kaisen Modulo . Illustrated by Yuji Iwasaki, the sequel featured some of the best visuals in Shonen Jump. Thanks to the popularity of the original, Modulo was another massive hit by Akutami. However, the sequel couldn’t fix the original ending. The story takes place 68 years after the Culling Game to center around new characters. However, instead of fixing the biggest questions of the original series, Modulo focused on an entirely new story with a sci-fi twist thanks to the introduction of Simurians, an alien race who came to Japan as refugees. The manga ran for six months, featuring some of the most exciting plot twists and battles, which is what makes Jujutsu Kaisen special.

There’s no denying that the finale was much more satisfying than the main story. However, it doesn’t change the fact that several things about the ritual and the future were left ambiguous . Not to mention that the sequel never revealed what happened to Megumi. He didn’t show up, unlike Nobara, which could only mean he died before the events of Modulo. However, his fate is still a mystery, especially since he was barely mentioned in the story. Additionally, the finale page itself was a cliffhanger when it teased that Dabura returned for Kyoko, since the manga already hinted that the two of them have feelings for each other. However, while it was more or less obvious, it would’ve been better to get an official confirmation, but the series didn’t confirm it at all.

What do you think about the finale of Jujutsu Kaisen and its sequel manga? Do you think the series deserves to return again and tie up the loose ends? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

title: 3 Anime to Watch If You Miss Demon Slayer
content:
Demon Slayer ‘s groundbreaking global success is primarily thanks to the anime adaptation by Ufotable. While the manga was already a decent enough success, the anime adaptation helped it reach new heights of popularity that few series had gotten before. Despite the initial controversies regarding the movie trilogy to adapt the Infinity Castle arc, the first installment was a historic success , and we can expect the same from the upcoming two movies as well. The Infinity Castle is the longest and most intense arc of the manga, where the Demon Slayer Corps engage in a battle against the Upper Moons.

It’s been more than a year since the first movie was released, but Ufotable has remained silent on the release window of the sequel. It’s more or less guaranteed at this point that the anime will return with the same visually stunning animation and intense fight sequences. However, if you’re looking to fill the void before the return of Demon Slayer, here are three anime you can stream now.

3) Dororo

As dark fantasies set in a historical Japanese period, both anime series focus on the protagonists fighting demons in order to regain something they have lost. Based on the 1967 manga by Osamu Tezuka, the story follows Hyakkimaru, whose father offered him to the demons even before he was born. In order to ensure the prosperity of his land, Daigo Kagemitsu, a greedy samurai lord, made a pact with 12 demons, which resulted in his son being born without limbs, a nose, eyes, ears, or even skin, yet he still survives. Disposed of and forgotten, the infant was saved by a kind man who creates prosthetics and weapons, allowing him to grow up. Hyakkimaru embarks on a journey to defeat the demons that took his body parts as sacrifices. During his journey, he befriends Dororo, an orphaned boy who tags along after being forced to fend for himself following his parents’ deaths.

2) Sword of the Demon Hunter: Kijin Gentosho

Even before the anime’s debut in March last year, many anime enthusiasts were discussing the similarities it shared with Demon Slayer . While the overall vibe is somewhat similar, both stories have somewhat different premises. The story follows Jinta, a shrine guardian whose duty is to eliminate any supernatural threats. However, it focuses on his journey as he continues to search for his childhood friend, Suzune, who was transformed into a demon by the divination. He travels around Japan across different eras and saves as many people as he can from the demons while hoping to cross paths with Suzune again.

1) Hell’s Paradise

While both anime have different premises, they are considered dark fantasies with intense action, visually striking animation, and protagonists who would go to any lengths for their loved ones. Hell’s Paradise follows Gabimaru , the strongest and most ruthless assassin from his village, Iwagakure. As he finds himself on death row, he gets one chance to gain his freedom. While initially reluctant to keep on living, he steels his resolve for his wife, Yui, who has been waiting for him to return. Unfortunately, the task entrusted to him is almost impossible to achieve since he is supposed to find a mythical Elixir of Life. To make things worse, it’s believed to be located on a mysterious island from which no one comes back alive. However, Gabimaru isn’t the only one who got a second chance; his fellow convicts are also looking for the same legendary elixir.

Do you agree with our picks – or have an anime you’d like to recommend that shares similar vibes to Demon Slayer ? Let us know in the comments below.

title: Light Novel 'Isekai Douraku ni Akitara' Gets TV Anime in Winter 2027
content:
Publishing company Shufunotomo announced a television anime adaptation of Fudaya Sanmongarasu and Tomozo 's Isekai Douraku ni Akitara ( Living It Up in Another World Until I Get Bored ) light novel on Friday. The anime series will premiere in January 2027.

Sanmongarasu began writing the adventure fantasy novel on the Shousetsuka ni Narou website in June 2016. Shufunotomo began printing the light novel under its Prime Novels imprint in June 2017, featuring illustrations by Tomozo. The imprint published two volumes, with the second volume released in April 2018. The series was later republished under the Hero Bunko imprint by Imagica Infos in January 2019. The seventh volume was published in October 2024. The eighth volume is scheduled for release on November 30, with its wraparound band featuring the anime announcement (pictured).

SAA began drawing a manga adaptation of the series on the Hero Comics web service in June 2025. The first volume was released digitally on September 30.

Hanashi Media licensed the light novel for English release under the title Living It Up in Another World Until I Get Bored , with the first volume scheduled for release on May 9, 2027.

Synopsis As if the universe heard him, his journey begins sooner than expected. On his way home, he suddenly finds himself stranded in another world-a strange, game-like place governed by levels, magic, skills, and other fantastical rules. And before he knows it, he's acquired tremendous power without even having to work for it.

With that kind of strength at his disposal, three paths lie before him: side with humanity and become a hero, join the demons and unleash chaos upon the world... or choose neither and use his newfound power for nothing more than his own amusement.

For him, the choice is obvious.

And so begins one thirty-something nobody's journey through another world, living exactly as he pleases until he gets bored! (Source: Hanashi Media)

Novel official page: https://herobunko.com/book/9242/

title: Bleach, Naruto & Classic Shonen Jump Anime Hits Are Now Easier to Stream Than Ever
content:
The golden age of Shonen during the 1990s and 2000s saw many promising shows in the industry, but very few could compete with the popularity of One Piece , Naruto , and Bleach . All three of these series eventually earned the title of the “Shonen Big Three,” as a testament to their popularity and unparalleled storylines not just in Shonen Jump , but in the entire demographic. While the term Big Three was completely fan-made, it highlighted the global influence and popularity of such shows. One Piece , being the oldest one , is still continuing, while Bleach and Naruto have long concluded their manga series. Bleach is all set to wrap up its main story this year, while Naruto’s spin-off manga, Boruto , is serializing its second part.

Launched in 1968, Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump eventually became the best-selling manga magazine of all time after serializing several memorable series, including Dragon Ball, One Piece, Naruto, Bleach , and many more. Even after all these decades, the magazine continues to stay on top with several hit series that redefine modern Shonen, including Jujutsu Kaisen and My Hero Academia . It’s also worth noting that among the 23 manga series in history that have sold more than 100 million copies, 12 of them were serialized in WSJ. Via a press release, some of the best Shonen Jump classics are easier to stream now than ever.

Bleach and Major Classics Confirm RetroCrush Streaming Release

Cineverse Announces Fresh Anime Classics Coming to RetroCrush as Part of its Fall Lineup. Popular franchises including BLEACH, Hunter x Hunter, Hikaru no Go, Pretty Guardian Sailor Moon, NARUTO, and more are now available or coming soon to RetroCrush. Cinverse, an entertainment technology company and studio, announced its upcoming slate of programming coming to its RetroCrush streaming service. This includes movies from BLEACH, Hunter x Hunter, Pretty Guardian Sailor Moon, NARUTO, as well as TV series such as Captain Tsubasa (2018), Hikaru no Go, and more.

The newest additions to RetroCrush feature TV and film titles including:

• BLEACH: Hell Verse (NOW AVAILABLE)

• Vampire Knight (NOW AVAILABLE)

• Genocyber (NOW AVAILABLE)

• Pretty Guardian Sailor Moon R Movie (NOW AVAILABLE)

• Sugar Sugar Rune (NOW AVAILABLE)

• Naruto the Movie: Ninja Clash in the Land of Snow (Streaming Nov. 13)

• Accel World (Streaming Nov. 13)

• Captain Tsubasa (Streaming Nov. 13 in English Dubbed and Dec. 4 in Original Japanese)

• Hunter X Hunter: Phantom Rouge (Streaming Nov. 20)

• Hikaru no Go (Streaming Nov. 27)

• The Girl Who Leapt Through Time (1983) (Streaming Dec. 4)

Naruto has officially confirmed an anime movie , and updates will be revealed sooner than expected. Viz Media revealed last weekend that a Naruto panel will be taking place on October 10th during the New York Comic Con 2026 event. NYCC is one of the largest fan conventions dedicated to Western comics, series, graphic novels, video games, anime, manga, and more. The convention was first held in 2006, and since then, it has welcomed hundreds of thousands of visitors each year.

title: Blue Rights Company Unveils Pilot Film for Orochi -Seventh Echoes- Original Animated Feature
content:
Entertainment company BLUE RIGHTS revealed on Friday a pilot film for its original feature-length animated movie titled OROCHI -Seventh Echoes- . The company also revealed the film's teaser visual and main staff. The pilot film features the theme song "Zankyo" performed by neNna .

BLUE RIGHTS describes the film's story:

Kukulkan is a kingdom sustained by sound waves. Born with a power known as “Hizumi,” Agni was abandoned by the royal family and grew up surrounded by his guardian and friends. His power awakens Orochi, a force of calamity believed to have died a thousand years ago. When Orochi awakens, he calls Agni “my son.” Who is Agni? What is this power for? To protect those he loves, the boy confronts the threat he has awakened. An epic adventure begins as sound and myth resonate together.

Takashi Nakamura ( Akira film character designer and animation director, A Tree of Palme , Harmony films director) is credited for the original concept and original character design, art setting, and is also directing the film. Tokuyuki Matsutake ( Medabots , Ninja vs. Gokudo , Tales of Phantasia ) is designing the characters.

Additional staff members include:

• In-Between Animation Supervisor: Mitsunori Murata

• Art Director: Kazuyuki Hashimoto

• Art Setting Assistant: Koji Hashiguchi

• Color Design: Terumi Nakauchi

• CGI Director: Keisuke Sasagawa (TRICK BLOCK)

Former MAPPA executive director, rights management director, and producer Makoto Kimura established BLUE RIGHTS in 2024, after he retired from his position at MAPPA . The announcement stated then that the company will produce televised and theatrical anime, as well as a range of entertainment outside anime, such as manga, novels, music, music videos, events, commercials, and products. The company prioritizes planning and production over animation production.

The company also revealed the film's teaser visual and main staff. The pilot film features the theme song "Zankyo" performed by neNna .
BLUE RIGHTS describes the film's story:

Kukulkan is a kingdom sustained by sound waves. Born with a power known as “Hizumi,” Agni was abandoned by the royal family and grew up surrounded by his guardian and friends. His power awakens Orochi, a force of calamity believed to have died a thousand years ago. When Orochi awakens, he calls Agni “my son.” Who is Agni? What is this power for? To protect those he loves, the boy confronts the threat he has awakened. An epic adventure begins as sound and myth resonate together.

title: Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 Confirms Release Date & Title With First Look
content:
Avatar: Seven Havens is wasting no time rolling out new episodes, with Season 2’s release dates already confirmed . Paramount+ got a certified hit on its hands this fall when the first batch of episodes for the latest in the Avatar franchise arrived, not only expanding the lore of the series in big ways but telling stories that no other show has been able to. Ahead of the series’ premiere, Paramount+ confirmed that Avatar: Seven Havens would return for two more seasons beyond the two that were already ordered and now we know that the wait won’t be long at all.

News of Avatar: Seven Havens Book 2 was officially confirmed today by Sehaj Sethi, the executive producer and developer of Avatar: Seven Havens , who confirmed the series will return on Friday, May 21, 2027. Paramount+ has also confirmed that the new season will once again have 13 episodes with a batch rollout too. Furthermore, the new episodes in Summer 2027 won’t be the last, as Book 3 of Avatar: Seven Havens will make its premiere later that year. Though no release window was given for Avatar: Seven Havens Book 4, it was confirmed it will be the final season of the series.

Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 Details Revealed

As noted, Avatar: Seven Havens Book 2 will debut on Friday, May 21, 2027, and, like the first season, will premiere with three episodes. Even though we’re six months away from the release of these episodes, Paramount+ has further confirmed the release dates for the rest of Season 2 as well, revealing that Episodes 4 – 6 will debut on May 28, Episode 7 – 9 on June 4, and Episodes 10 – 13 on June 11. Assuming the same timeline holds for Book 3, it could very well make its premiere this time next year as well.

In Book 2, entitled ‘Discovery’, Pavi continues her chakra journey to the Floating Isles and learns more about what happened to Korra. Meanwhile, Nisha discovers vital information about the mysterious spirit energy Pavi released from Ellora. The girls are brought together in New Ba Sing Se, along with all their unresolved issues.

Avatar: Seven Havens Book 2 will see returning cast Saheli Khan as Pavi, Aishu Devan as Nisha, Akshay Khanna as Karthik, Major Curda as Jae, Sakina Jaffrey as Agam, Darren Barnet as Daemin, and Dee Bradley Baker as Geet and Ruhi.

News of Avatar: Seven Havens Book 2’s premiere date wasn’t the only thing revealed by Sehaj Sethi during the AMA, though, as they confirmed that the planned four books of the series was their intention from the beginning. She added, “Mike, Bryan, and I knew from the beginning where the series was going. We developed the show with an overarching storyline in mind.”

“Mike and Bryan set up the concept and we basically had free reign within the parameters they set up,” Ethan Spaulding, Executive Producer added. “Creatively we were free to expand/explore visually and story-wise, Mike and Bryan would always reign us in if we went too far astray. So, yes Mike and Bryan were involved in everything.”

This is a developing story.

title: Ace Needs His Own One Piece Spin-Off Anime
content:
Fire Fist Portgas D. Ace’s tragic death at Marineford eliminated one of One Piece ‘s fan-favorite characters almost 700 episodes before its current timeline . Monkey D. Luffy lost a key piece of his family when Admiral Akainu killed his adopted brother. Unlike a lot of manga and anime, he didn’t return either. There was no resuscitation, a multiverse, or anything to bring him back and that’s what makes that scene so shocking and captivating after all these years.

However, two small novels ( One Piece Ace’s Story: Formation of the Spade Pirates and One Piece Ace’s Story: New World ) released in 2018 and gave fans a prequel glimpse of Ace’s life and ascension to captain of the Spade Pirates. Eiichiro Oda didn’t write the stories, but was involved in the supervision of the project. This means that the story sits in the official canon timeline. Although no content is set up for Ace’s future, the prequel stories give an opportunity to detail his past on screen. One Piece ‘s next movie should absolutely make these two volumes into a film, or even create a short series that can go beyond the novels.

Ace Of Flames Changes Family Legacy

A bit of a spoiler alert, but the two novels quickly tell how Ace and the Spade Pirates came to be . The first novel explores Ace’s upbringing and pirate roots going back to his father Gol D. Roger. Ace and his first crew member Deuce are stranded on an island, but eventually escape through building a ship, but not before Ace unknowingly eats the Flame-Flame Fruit to gain his powers.

The duo eventually escape and from there and begin a journey much like his brother’s. Ace is a pirate, but certainly doesn’t act like one. In the novels, he regularly goes out of his way to help the innocent and even rivals like Marine Ensign Isuka. His behavior dispels any notion that he’s exactly like his father. In fact, he commits wholeheartedly to showing everyone around him that his heritage doesn’t define him. Ace wants to chart his own path to pirate glory.

A Heroic Life Cut Short Deserves More Lore

The dichotomy in Ace’s and Luffy’s approaches is what makes anime like One Piece so intriguing, and their characters so likable . While they’re pirates, which is usually synonymous with heinous acts like pillaging and murdering, both protect the vulnerable, show deep loyalty to their friends and family, and are only guilty of fighting and resisting establishment authority.

His father’s life was cut short for his many crimes, but Ace’s was ended for defending his brother. One Piece fans continue to follow Luffy’s journey to the top of the pirating world, but lost the chance to see how Ace’s career would turn out. It only makes sense that they’d at least get to see the genesis of his pirate life. Would you like to see more Ace content in One Piece ? Let us know in the comments.

title: Pokémon’s First Movie Is Still Peak Even After 27 Years
content:
With the number of anime series and movies Pokémon has released over the years, fans often find themselves celebrating major milestones throughout the year. However, there’s something special about the first movie that just can’t be beat. Pokémon has released several anime seasons, movies, card games, video games, manga, and more, all of which contributed to the long-standing popularity of the franchise. For many 1990s kids, the series is a nostalgic childhood memory as it takes the viewers into a fantasy world full of unique and adorable creatures. Based on the popular 1996 video game, the renowned Japanese animation studio OLM released an anime series a year later.

The story primarily follows Ash Ketchum on his journey to become the greatest Pokémon master ever, but later on, several spin-offs also focused on other characters. Every new season or movie of the story takes fans on a completely new adventure regardless of whether it’s a film or a season. The anime has released 23 movies over the decades, but the first one can’t be compared with anything else. Pokémon: The First Movie – Mewtwo Strikes Back premiered in the U.S. on November 12th, 1999, more than a year after the Japanese premiere. It’s been 27 years since the anime movie was introduced to fans in the U.S., and it’s now considered a timeless classic with a plot and storytelling that new fans can enjoy even now.

What Is the First Pokémon Movie About?

Directed by Kunihiko Yuyama, the film was initially released in Japan before making its English debut for fans in the U.S. It’s based on an original story set outside of the TV anime show, which was airing the Indigo League at the time of the original release in 1998. However, the story was still connected to the main plot as it took a short detour during the journey of Ash Ketchum and his friends. While on his way to compete in the World-Class Tournament, Ash’s group crossed paths with Mew and Mewtwo, two legendary Pokémon . Both of these Pokémons were introduced for the first time in the franchise’s history and later became iconic thanks to the movie’s popularity.

The movie reveals that Team Rocket managed to create the first successful clone by using the fossil of the Legendary Pokémon Mew. The story primarily centers around the clone, who was named Mewtwo, a man-made version of one of the most powerful creatures of all time that quickly becomes aware of the circumstances it was created under. After waking up, Mewtwo realizes that its creators only see it as a weapon and goes on a rampage. It fled after destroying the laboratory but crossed paths with Sakaki, the leader of Team Rocket, who manipulates the cloned Pokémon into committing all kinds of atrocities.

It doesn’t take long for Mewtwo to become repulsed by the cruelty of mankind and isolate itself. Mewtwo tries to plot against humans while also hoping to find its true purpose in life. While disguising itself as the world’s strongest Pokémon trainer, Mewtwo accepts the challenges from new trainers from across the regions. However, Mewtwo’s life begins to shift when it encounters Ash and the others who will do anything to stop it from destroying humanity.

Pokémon: The First Movie – Mewtwo Strikes Back Still Holds Up Today

The movie was released when the anime was at the peak of its popularity , which is why it helped pave the path for the franchise’s long-time success. Not only that, but the plot and the character depth of Mewtwo can never get boring no matter how many times you watch it. Although the movie was marketed towards a young audience, it portrayed profound philosophical depth, which was pretty unexpected considering the movie was based on an original story. Mewtwo Strikes Back isn’t simply loved for its original storytelling, but because of the complex themes it explored.

Ash’s sacrifice and the heartbreaking reaction of Pikachu are still considered one of the saddest moments in the entire series. Not to mention that Mewtwo later became a considerably crucial character in the franchise’s history, which is all the more reason why the film’s legacy carried on even now. It may not be objectively the best anime movie of the franchise since fan preferences can vary depending on many factors. However, whether it’s nostalgia, the classic animation style of the 1990s, the movie will always be irreplaceable.

Do you think the first movie is still the best after all these years, or do you have another personal favorite? Let us know in the comments below!
